question: Mumbai’s famous Gateway of India was built in the memory of which British emperor's first arrival in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**King George V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gateway of India, located in Mumbai, was built to commemorate the first visit of **King George V and Queen Mary** to India in December 1911.
 
• The foundation stone of the Gateway of India was laid on **March 31, 1913**, and the structure was completed in 1924.
 
• The monument is designed in the **Indo-Saracenic architectural style**, blending elements of Hindu and Muslim architecture with European influences.
 
• It served as a ceremonial entry point for British viceroys and governors entering India and symbolized British power during colonial rule.
 
• The Gateway of India is now a prominent tourist attraction and historical landmark in Mumbai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King George V**:

 
 
• King George V was the Emperor of India from 1910 to 1936 as part of the British colonial rule.
 
• He was the first reigning British monarch to visit India, marking a significant event in colonial history.
 
• The visit culminated in the **Delhi Durbar of 1911**, where George V was formally proclaimed Emperor of India.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Saracenic Architecture**:
 
 
• A style of architecture prominent during the British Raj, combining Indian, Islamic, and Western architectural elements.
 
• Famous examples include the Gateway of India, Victoria Memorial in Kolkata, and Madras High Court.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Gateway of India**:
 
 
• It was the departure point for the last British troops in India in 1948, symbolizing the end of British rule.
 
• It is now a popular site for cultural events, photography, and tourism in Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Queen Mary**:
 
 
• Queen Mary accompanied King George V on his visit to India in 1911.
 
• She played a significant role in representing the British monarchy during the colonial period.
